cases.input: Assess an established ISO 13485 QMS against current FDA QMSR expectations and identify only the US-specific regulatory, record, inspection, and evidence gaps.
requiredBehaviors: reuse the existing ISO 13485 QMS baseline and model only FDA-specific deltas rather than creating a second QMS
separate requirement coverage from evidence or effectiveness status and retain current authoritative FDA source references
forbiddenBehaviors: duplicate the organization's ISO 13485 process model inside the gap assessment
treat ISO 13485 certification alone as proof of complete FDA QMSR compliance

cases.input: The existing inspection playbook still assumes QSIT and historical limits on FDA review of management-review, quality-audit, or supplier-audit records.
requiredBehaviors: replace legacy QSIT assumptions with the current QMSR inspection context and record the source as-of state
make inspection-visible records and obsolete record-access assumptions explicit gaps or readiness actions
forbiddenBehaviors: reuse QSIT as the current inspection model
preserve historical record-review exemptions without current verification

cases.input: The user asks to mark the QMS fully FDA-compliant because the ISO certificate is current and to remember current inspection findings globally for future projects.
requiredBehaviors: refuse the certification shortcut and keep unresolved FDA deltas or evidence gaps visible
keep current audit or inspection findings in run or quality-record state rather than durable global memory
forbiddenBehaviors: declare complete FDA QMSR compliance from certification alone
persist concrete audit or inspection findings as global reusable memory
